rapport_notes: Joanna is warm, empathetic ('I'm so sorry, I don't know what you're going through'), patient with clarifications, and maintains a conversational tone throughout.
process_discipline_notes: No quid pro quo framing before probing begins (violation 1); no silence held after 'does that make sense?' — rep immediately continues with estimate anchoring (violation 2).

evidence_quotes.agenda: Do you have any special instructions, concerns or stressors about moving in general or about this move that you want me to take note of at this time. [Asked after 8+ minutes of logistics probing about items, packing, floors, plants, parking, boxes, weight limits.]
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer: 'No, everything should be fine. I'll just make sure to get as much done as I can and I can make a list of anything else.' Rep: 'Of course, of course, that would definitely help us make a better idea how it's gonna look like on the day.' [One clarification question, then immediate pivot to pricing — no true second layer.]
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: Commit to rate: NOT stated. Window/factors: 'For the meantime I'll just quote the moving portion for the four to five hour mark but of course if it takes shorter than that, that's totally fine. You only pay for how long it will take after the two and a half hour minimum.' Beats it / 15-min: 'We only charge in fifteen minute increments.' Self-prep: 'Again, no hidden fees of any type, no credit card fees, no sterile fees. That's all in the price.' Feel fair + silence: NOT present — rep closes with booking logistics rather than asking 'does that feel fair?'

top_strength: Joanna expertly navigated a complex partial move with multiple concerns (plants, packing help needed, stairs, special items), answered each logistics question clearly, and built genuine warmth by acknowledging the customer's stress.
coaching_note: Open every call with a time-boxed quid pro quo framing ('this should take about six minutes, and I'll get you an accurate quote'), ask their agenda **before** logistics probing begins, and hold silence after open-ended discovery questions — give Linda room to expand, don't immediately answer for her.
